title: Impact on Singapore of Phase Three of US Rebalancing Strategy
what_it_is: Impact on Singapore of Phase Three of US Rebalancing Strategy

sections.label: US Rebalancing and Singapore security
sections.summary: Singapore partners like-minded countries and helped set up the ADMM-Plus in 2010, while remaining responsible for its own security.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Defence (a) what does Phase Three of the US Rebalancing Strategy entail for Singapore and the region in terms of security; (b) what is the Government's assessment of the associated security benefits, costs, and risks; and (c) how does the Government intend to maximise these gains while addressing the costs and mitigating the risks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: We, Singaporeans, are ultimately responsible for our own security but we will partner like-minded countries that pursue common objectives of peace and stability for our region.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: For this reason, Singapore joined the Five Power Defence Arrangements (FPDA) in 1971 which imposes an obligation on the five nations to consult in the event of an external attack on Malaysia and Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: In the past decade, we have also worked with other ASEAN countries to build a security architecture that is inclusive and based on the rule of law; where peaceful settlement of disputes, dialogue, cooperation and non-provocation are the norm for countries within that framework.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: This led to the set-up of ASEAN Defence Ministers' Meeting (ADMM)-Plus in 2010, which includes, apart from the ASEAN member states, China, India, Japan, South Korea, Australia and New Zealand from Asia, as well as the US and Russia.

sections.label: US defence agreements with Singapore
sections.summary: A 1990 MOU, updated by the 2005 Strategic Framework Agreement and enhanced Defence Cooperation Agreement in 2015, facilitated US presence.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: US ships and planes are more frequent users since the 1990 Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) was signed by our founding Prime Minister, Mr Lee Kuan Yew, and then-US Vice President Dan Quayle.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: That MOU facilitated the US' presence in this region and provided the security umbrella under which emerging economies in Asia thrived.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: The MOU was updated by the Strategic Framework Agreement by Prime Minister Lee and then-US President George W Bush in 2005.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: And recently, we enhanced the Defence Cooperation Agreement with the US in 2015.

sections.label: FPDA and US agreements
sections.summary: Singapore cites the 1971 FPDA and its MOU, Strategic Framework Agreement and enhanced DCA with the US as working with like-minded countries.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: I mentioned the FPDA in 1971; there is a historical basis, but it also falls in line with this overarching principle that we will work with like-minded countries that seek peace and stability in our region.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: We also have an MOU, a Strategic Framework Agreement and an enhanced DCA with the US, which facilitates the use of their ships and planes in our airbases.
